calls.overall_summary: Apple reported products revenue growth of 2% and services revenue growth of 14%, alongside revenue declines of 11% in Greater China and 2% in Wearables, Home and Accessories. Management reported stronger year-over-year iPhone 16 family performance in markets with Apple Intelligence and expected March-quarter total company revenue growth in the low to mid-single digits. FinBERT classified 24.2% of scored transcript segments as positive, 3.2% as negative and 72.5% as neutral; these labels do not measure investor sentiment.

The call highlighted solid top‑line growth, with M365 consumer and commercial products, cloud services, and LinkedIn all posting double‑digit or low‑double‑digit increases, and operating margins improving modestly. However, pressure on cash flow, on‑premises server sales, enterprise services, and cloud gross margins tempered the outlook. Overall sentiment was 30% positive, 4.7% negative, and 65.2% neutral according to FinBERT.

The earnings call showed robust overall and automotive revenue growth and high margins, while gaming sales fell and the China business weakened. Sentiment was heavily neutral (81.0%) with modest positive (16.9%) and minimal negative (2.1%) tones.

The call highlighted strong ad revenue growth in key geographies and increased marketing, R&D, and cost of revenue driven by infrastructure spending, reflecting a largely positive outlook. However, declines were noted in Meta Quest sales, government and politics, gaming, and G&A expenses, contributing to a predominantly neutral sentiment with 26.1% positive, 3.2% negative, and 70.7% neutral sentiment overall.
